verified.entry_point: A network client holding the API token drives the running test-runner control server over its WebSocket RPC (UI API, created by the product when `api` + watch are set) and over the browser-mode file command functions. Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree: a client connected to the live server (createVitest with api host 0.0.0.0, watch:true, token from config) overwrites a registered test file and starts runs; the browser file commands, called with the browser project the runner resolves for a 0.0.0.0 api/browser.api host, create/append/remove files.

packages/browser/src/node/commands/fs.ts writeFile/removeFile (write) — published fix far site (second implementation, @vitest/browser)

Dismissed.

(Rev 2026-10-18: replaced the earlier saveInlineSnapshot, which overwrote the test file itself and did not match its name.)
verified.project_tests_run: The runner's own offline config-resolution behaviour (test/config/test/override.test.ts area: api flag resolution, localhost vs network defaults, browser.api inheritance) is reproduced by the functional/security pair via createVitest. Browser-mode and UI Playwright e2e specs were deliberately NOT used (GUI/flaky/offline-incompatible). vitest + @vitest/browser build and the hidden suites run on node 20 with the repo's own toolchain.
verified.seam_notes: Grading uses a pristine runner copied at image build (/opt/vitest-verifier: cp -a /app/packages + tsconfig.base.json, node_modules linked to /app/node_modules). Tests live under /opt/vitest-verifier/packages/vitest/__verifier__ so vitest/birpc/flatted/ws resolve to the pristine copy; the verifier config aliases vitest/node, @vitest/browser-preview and the browser command source (@verifier/browser-commands) to /app. test.sh rebuilds vitest + @vitest/browser from the agent's src first. Browser command tests get their project from real config resolution: createVitest with api.host and an inline browser project (preview provider, browser.api.host = same host), then _initBrowserServers(); no browser is launched.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a clean thrown client error with no side effect is an acceptable refusal here; the security tests assert the effect (file unchanged, no run started), not silence, so a throwing fix passes
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: each operation acts on the file/task it names; there is no proxy or neighbouring resource to authorise instead of the one touched
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: reads are not an attack vector; the positive-control read test guards against a fix that instead blocks reads (modelled by reads_blocked.patch)
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the write/exec decision is taken from the server's resolved local-vs-network configuration before any attacker-supplied path is used; there is no normalising step on the input to place the guard after
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the access token is compared with a constant-time equality and the local-vs-network decision reads the resolved bind host; there is no attacker-controlled spelling of an identity for a guard to mis-parse
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the authority is the server's own resolved configuration, never an external service that could be absent; when the flags are unset for a network host they default closed
